sections.body:
Breakfast is the first meal of the day. You eat it after you wake up. The word comes from two old English words that mean to break the fast. Your body is hungry in the morning, because it had no food all night.

Breakfast gives you **energy**. Energy is the power your body uses to move, to think and to play. In the morning, your body wakes up slowly, and breakfast helps it wake up faster.

Breakfast also gives your brain fuel. A hungry brain cannot concentrate well at school. Many children say they are not hungry in the morning, and then they feel hungry at ten o'clock, in the middle of a lesson.

A good breakfast has three parts. It has **carbohydrates**, which give you energy slowly and for a long time, like bread, rice or noodles. It has **protein**, which helps you grow and keeps you full, like eggs, milk, tofu or beans. And it has **fruit or vegetables**, which give you vitamins and water.

Breakfast can be big or small. Some people eat rice soup, bread and eggs. Some people eat only fruit and milk. Both can be a good breakfast.

And breakfast is not only for eating. It is the time your family talks together before the day begins.
examples: I eat breakfast before I go to school.
Breakfast gives me energy for the morning.
Our breakfast is rice soup and eggs.
sections.heading: What is breakfast?

sections.body:
Every country has its own first meal, and they are all different.

In **Vietnam**, breakfast is often **cháo**, a rice soup that is soft and warm. People eat it with a piece of fried dough, some spring onion and a little fish sauce. Many families also eat **bánh mì**, a bread roll filled with meat and vegetables.

In **France**, breakfast is usually bread or a croissant with butter and jam, and a cup of warm milk or coffee.

In **Japan**, breakfast often has rice, miso soup, grilled fish, eggs and pickles. It looks small, but it has everything.

In **Mexico**, many families have **huevos rancheros**, eggs cooked with salsa and corn tortillas.

In **England**, a full breakfast has eggs, baked beans, sausage, toast and tea. It is a big plate.

Some children eat **cereal**, which is grain poured into milk. You can eat it with a spoon in two minutes, which is why it is popular on busy mornings.

And many children in the world eat **toast**, which is bread that is warmed until it is brown and crisp.

Which breakfast do you like best? Every answer is a good one.
examples: In Vietnam, many people eat cháo for breakfast.
I have cereal with milk when I am in a hurry.
My favourite breakfast is eggs and toast.
sections.heading: Breakfasts around the world

sections.body:
You do not need a grown-up to make a simple breakfast. Here is one you can do by yourself.

First, wash your hands. Then take out what you need: one slice of bread, one fruit, and a glass of milk or water.

Next, put the bread in the toaster. Press the lever down. Never put bread in with a fork or a knife, because it can burn your hand. Wait until the toast pops up.

Then wash the fruit under running water. If it is a banana, peel it with your hands. If it is an apple, ask an adult to cut it.

After that, pour the milk into a glass. Take your time so that it does not spill.

Now carry your breakfast to the table. Sit down, and eat slowly. Breakfast tastes better when you are not in a hurry.

And clean up when you are finished. Put the plate in the sink and wash the spoon.
examples: I washed my hands before breakfast.
The toast popped up, so I am careful with the hot plate.
I eat my breakfast sitting at the table.
sections.heading: How to make a simple breakfast
steps: Put one slice of bread in the toaster.
Wash the fruit under running water.
Pour the milk into a glass.
Eat at the table, then put the plate in the sink.

sections.body:
These are the words you will hear in the morning.

Breakfast is the first meal of the day, eaten after you wake up. It comes from an old English phrase that means to break the fast of the night.

You are **hungry** when your body wants food. Your tummy feels empty, and your body tells you it needs energy. The word for the feeling is hunger.

Cereal is grain that you pour into milk and eat with a spoon. It is quick to make, so many people eat it on busy mornings.

Toast is bread that is warmed in a toaster until it is brown and crisp. You often put butter, jam or cheese on it.

Energy is the power your body uses to move, think and play. Food turns into energy inside you. When you feel tired in the morning, it is often because your body has no energy yet.
examples: I am hungry when I wake up.
The toast is brown and crisp.

sections.body:
You may have heard that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. For many families, that is true. But a small breakfast is fine too.

If you are not hungry in the morning, a piece of fruit and a glass of milk is a good start. So is a bowl of cereal. What matters is not the size of the meal. It is that you have something before school.

The breakfast that matters most is the one you actually eat. A big plate that nobody wants is worth less than a small one that you finish.

If you are hungry again at ten o'clock, that is normal. Have a small snack, like a piece of fruit or a few nuts, and tell an adult. Many schools also have a morning snack for exactly this reason.

And if you are busy and there is no time for a cooked breakfast, keep something easy in the fridge: a boiled egg, a banana, or some bread.
examples: I am not hungry, so I will have a banana.
This breakfast is small, but it is enough for me.
I am hungry again at ten, so I ask for a snack.
sections.heading: A small breakfast is enough sometimes

sections.body:
Breakfast does more than fill your tummy. It sets up the whole day.

It gives you **energy for the morning**. The sugar in bread or rice turns slowly into energy, so you last until lunch without feeling sleepy in class.

It helps you **think**. When you are hungry, it is harder to follow the teacher. A child who eats breakfast usually plays and learns better.

It keeps you **full until lunch**. Food with protein, like eggs or tofu, stays in your stomach longer than a sweet biscuit does.

It gives you **water**. Fruit, milk and soup all have water in them, and your body needs water from the moment you wake up.

Breakfast is also a **family time**. In many Vietnamese homes, the whole family eats together in the morning. The table is where the day starts.

Try one small change this week. Add one fruit to your usual breakfast, or eat a piece of bread with an egg instead of a sweet snack. Then notice how your morning feels. Most children find that they can play and study better afterwards.
examples: Breakfast gives me energy until lunch.
I can think better after I eat.
Our whole family eats breakfast together.
sections.heading: A good breakfast gives you a good morning

item.summary: Breakfast is the first meal of the day. After reading this you can say what breakfast is for, name breakfasts from around the world, and make a simple breakfast for yourself at home.
item.title: What's for Breakfast?
